agent: wave 13 agent B - CEffect slot 12, and the six resource triggers' goods pool
question: What is CEffect slot 12 (the five bodies the effect family's scalar middles supply), and does a government in exile read its host's goods or its own - and which province's?
slots_noted:
**There is no `CEffect` slot 12.** `CEffect`'s own table has twelve slots; five of its *siblings* among the abstract middles each declare their own first virtual, which therefore lands at index 12 in every table below them. The partition is exact and total: of the 111-class family, 58 tables have 12 slots and 43 have 13, and the 43 split 24/11/2/2/4 by RTTI base - every `CIntEffect` heir holds 0x59D4F0, every `CValueEffect` heir 0x59CB90, both `CBoolEffect` heirs 0x59DC90, both `CStringEffect` heirs 0x59E220, and the four classes that derive straight from `CEffect` and still have 13 slots (CWarEffect, CWarGoalEffect, CModifySpiesEffect, CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect) hold 0x5BD110. The two groups are not even the same function: the four scalar-middle bodies are `ret 0xc` text builders and 0x5BD110 is `ret 8` and answers a CCountryTag, so one slot index carries two unrelated signatures and a virtual call through it is only safe behind a known middle class. The four scalar bodies are therefore named for the middle that owns them (`CIntEffect::FormatValueText` and the three siblings), and the slot is recorded on the middle so it propagates to all 43 tables.

**0x5BD110 is deliberately left class-free, as `Effect_GetTargetCountryTag`.** It is in four tables, all at slot 12, and RTTI gives the four classes no common ancestor but `CEffect` - whose table has no slot 12 at all. So it is a four-way linker fold of four identical source bodies and naming it for any one of the four would be trap 4; the slot is still recorded for all four. `CEffect +0x20`/`+0x24` is a `CCountryTag` on these four classes, but `+0x20` is where every subclass's own data starts, so that is not a `CEffect` field and no struct field is recorded for it. `CBoolEffect +0x20` is a bool (`cmp byte ptr [esi+0x20], 0` at 0x59DCCD) and `CStringEffect`'s slot 12 never reads its own data at all; neither is recorded for the same reason.

No struct fields are recorded. Everything the six resource triggers touch was already in the fact base - `CCountry +0x95 government_in_exile`, `CCountry +0x9F8 pool_in_exile`, `CCountry +0xE24 acting_capital_province_id`, `CMapProvince +0x15C pool` and all seven `CGoodsPool` fields - and this reading is six-way corroboration of the `CGoodsPool` layout rather than a first settlement of any of it. `CEffect +0x14` is still untouched by anything read here.

addresses.name: CIntEffect::FormatValueText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CIntEffect::FormatValueText(CIntEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString* key)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 12, and the biggest of the five bodies the effect family's scalar middles supply - 24 holders, every `CIntEffect` heir, nobody overriding it.** 0x59D4F0 to the single `ret 0xc` at 0x59DC47, 0x75A bytes, four int3 before (the previous function is `CIntEffect::TakeScalarValue` at 0x59D4A0) and nine after.

It renders *the caller's* localisation key with the effect's own number substituted into it: `GetText (0x682490)` on `key`, then four replacements added to that `CInternationalizedText` and `CInternationalizedText::Render (0x682E40)` into `out`, which is returned in EAX.

| token | what goes in |
| --- | --- |
| `$VALUE$` | a colour run - `§Y`, then `§G` if `this->+0x20 > 0` and `§R` if `< 0` and nothing when it is exactly 0 - then **`abs(value / 1000)`** as a plain integer (`imul 0x10624DD3; sar edx,6`, then the `cdq/xor/sub` absolute-value idiom, then `_itoa` at 0x79A0C4), then `§W` |
| `$DIRECTION$` | `GetText("GAIN")` when `+0x20 >= 0`, `GetText("LOSE")` otherwise - so the sign is carried by the word and the colour, never by the digits |
| `$WHERE$` | `g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790) ->provinces (+0xB8C) [scope->province (+0x28)]`, then slot 7 of that province's second vftable at `+8`, coloured `§Y`. **Unguarded**: nothing tests whether the scope has a province, so on a country-scoped effect this names province 0 |

The `/1000` is the exact inverse of `CIntEffect::TakeScalarValue`'s `atoi(text) * 1000`, which is the control on the scale.

**Nothing in the image calls it.** See the evidence; `CValueEffect`'s identical body has two callers and this one has none, so the 24 `CIntEffect` leaves - which include all seven `*PoolEffect` classes - each duplicate these substitutions inside their own slot 9 instead. The name is BiceLib's, from what the body does and from the two call sites of the sibling body.
addresses.evidence: Body decoded end to end from the vftable entry (so the entry is an entry by definition, not a `functionStart` guess); one `ret 0xc` and the signature's three stack dwords agree. Slot membership read as `vftable + 12*4` out of the RTTI tables for all 101 family classes with a table: 24 hold this address, all at slot 12, and all 24 have `CIntEffect` as their RTTI base. `$VALUE$`/`$DIRECTION$`/`$WHERE$`/`GAIN`/`LOSE` read as string operands at 0x59D585, 0x59D7B7, 0x59D967, 0x59D725, 0x59D774. The `/1000` idiom at 0x59D5B7-0x59D5CC. The 'nothing calls it' negative is two scans: (a) every `mov r32,[r32+0x30]` in .text followed by `call` on the same register, 464 sites, of which the three inside the effect module VA 0x99C000-0x9C2000 all have a non-effect receiver (`[edi+0x5C]`/`[edi+0x64]` neighbours); (b) every slot body of all 43 thirteen-slot family classes, bounded by its own padding run, scanned for a `+0x30` dispatch. **Positive control for both:** the same two scans find 0x59CB90's two callers (CWarexhaustionEffect::GetText at 0x59E9F4 and CRevoltRiskEffect::GetText at 0x5A5654) and all nine call sites of 0x5BD110. A scan for the one-instruction `call dword ptr [reg+0x30]` form finds zero of them anywhere in the image, so the two-instruction scan is not missing an encoding. Shown wrong by: a caller that reaches it with a `CEffect*` receiver from outside the family - a decision or event tooltip builder is where to look - or any substitution token beyond the four.

addresses.name: CValueEffect::FormatValueText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CValueEffect::FormatValueText(CValueEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString* key)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 12 for all eleven `CValueEffect` heirs**, and the only one of the five whose callers are known. 0x59CB90 to the single `ret 0xc` at 0x59D494, 0x905 bytes, nine int3 after; the byte before the entry is a single int3 and the function above it is `CValueEffect::TakeScalarValue` at 0x59CB50, which is the known trap 2 pair.

Same shape as `CIntEffect::FormatValueText` - `GetText` on the caller's key, replacements, `CInternationalizedText::Render` - with the same `$DIRECTION$` and `$WHERE$`, a decimal `$VALUE$`, and one token the integer form does not have:

| token | what goes in |
| --- | --- |
| `$VALUE$` | the colour run, then **`fabs(value / 1000.0)`** to **two** decimal places (`cvtdq2ps`, `divsd` by the 1000.0 at 0x160A300, `fabs` through 0x40C390, format through 0x65AEC0 with precision 2) |
| `$PERC$` | the value read as a **multiplier**: `(value/1000.0 - 1.0) * 100`, to **one** decimal place, with a literal `+` prefix when positive and nothing when not, then `%§W`. So 1.25 renders `+25.0%` and 0.8 renders `-20.0%`. Unlike `$VALUE$` this keeps its sign |
| `$DIRECTION$` | `GetText("GAIN")`/`GetText("LOSE")` on the sign of `+0x20` |
| `$WHERE$` | the scope's province, through the game state, unguarded - as in the integer form |

Its two callers are its whole purpose and both are three lines long: `CWarexhaustionEffect::GetText` (0x59E9A0) and `CRevoltRiskEffect::GetText` (0x5A5600) build one `Hoi3CString` of their own keyword's key and hand it straight to this slot. The other nine `CValueEffect` leaves - `CDissentEffect::GetText` at 0x5BA110 is the clearest - inline the same `GetText`/`$VALUE$`/replacement sequence by hand instead, which is why a slot the whole family declares has two users.

The name is BiceLib's, from the body and from those two call sites.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from the vftable entry; one `ret 0xc`, three stack dwords, they agree. Eleven holders, all at slot 12, all with `CValueEffect` as their RTTI base - and the eleven are exactly the eleven holders of `CValueEffect::TakeScalarValue` that FINDINGS-effects.md already counted. `$PERC$` arithmetic read at 0x59CFCA-0x59D097: `movd xmm0,[this+0x20]`, `/1000.0`, `subsd` the 1.0 at 0x160A248, `comiss` the 0.0 at 0x15BED10 choosing the `+` at 0x15BC244 or the shared empty string at 0x15B4945, `mulsd` the 100.0 at 0x160A358, precision 1. `fabs` confirmed by decoding 0x40C390, which is `fld; fabs; fstp`. The two callers are a complete scan of every slot body of all 43 thirteen-slot classes for a `+0x30` dispatch, with the arguments read at the sites: `push <local key>; push [ebp+0xC]; push [ebp+8]; mov ecx,esi; call eax`, which also fixes the argument order. Shown wrong by: a third caller, or a `$PERC$` consumer in the localisation files that reads it as a plain percentage rather than as a deviation from 1.

addresses.name: CBoolEffect::FormatValueText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CBoolEffect::FormatValueText(CBoolEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString* key)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 12 for `CBoolEffect`'s two heirs**, `CFixedAIStrategyEffect` and `CFormGovernmentInExileAction`. 0x59DC90 to the single `ret 0xc` at 0x59E1C3, 0x536 bytes, ten int3 after.

The same `GetText(key)` / replacements / `Render` shape as the integer and value forms, with only two tokens, because a bool has no number to print: `$DIRECTION$` is `GetText("GAIN")` when `this->+0x20` is non-zero and `GetText("LOSE")` when it is zero (`cmp byte ptr [esi+0x20], bl` at 0x59DCCD - so `CBoolEffect`'s value is a **byte**), and `$WHERE$` is the scope's province through the game state, unguarded, as in the other two.

No caller: both heirs' slot 9 does its own text. `inferred` rather than `confirmed` because the role rests on the body being the same construction as two siblings whose callers are known, not on a call site of its own.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from the vftable entry; one `ret 0xc` and three stack dwords agree. Two holders, both at slot 12, both with `CBoolEffect` as their RTTI base, and those are `CBoolEffect`'s only two heirs with a table - so this is the base's own body inherited twice, not a fold. `GAIN`/`LOSE`/`DIRECTION`/`WHERE` read as string operands at 0x59DCD4, 0x59DD20, 0x59DD62, 0x59DF1F; no `VALUE` and no `PERC` anywhere in the body. No caller: the whole-image two-instruction `+0x30` dispatch scan and the per-slot scan of all 43 holders, both with the positive control that they find 0x59CB90's two callers and 0x5BD110's nine. Shown wrong by: a call site, or `CBoolEffect +0x20` turning out to be wider than a byte.

addresses.name: CStringEffect::FormatValueText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CStringEffect::FormatValueText(CStringEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString* key)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 12 for `CStringEffect`'s two heirs, and the whole body is the developers saying not to.** 0x59E220 to the single `ret 0xc` at 0x59E24D, 0x2E bytes, and it is nine instructions: `*out = "DON'T CALL THIS ONE"` (the string at 0x15F39D0, through `std::string::assign` at 0xA160) and return `out`. Neither the scope nor the key is read.

It is the fifth of the five slot-12 bodies and the one that explains the other four: the virtual is declared independently on five sibling middles, and the middle whose value is a string has nothing to substitute, so its implementation is a loud marker rather than a silent empty one. `CLoadOOBEffect` and `CRemoveBrigadeEffect` - `CStringEffect`'s only two heirs - both inherit it and neither calls it.

**Trap 2, a new pair:** the `ret 0xc` at 0x59E24D is followed with **no padding at all** by a fresh `push ebp` at 0x59E250, which is an effect constructor (`ret 0x108`, a `CToken` by value, writing the vftable at VA 0x15F445C and `CPersistent::token` 0x18D). So `functionStart(0x59E250)` answers 0x59E220 and `retsBefore` reports one unexplained `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Nine instructions decoded from the vftable entry to the one `ret 0xc`; the string operand at 0x59E236 is 0x15F39D0, which reads "DON'T CALL THIS ONE" with length 0x13 pushed alongside it. Two holders, both at slot 12, both `CStringEffect` heirs, and the RTTI export gives `CStringEffect` exactly those two derived classes. That `CStringEffect` itself declares the slot rather than the two leaves separately is settled by the heirs of the *other* string-shaped middles: `CFlagEffect`'s six and `CVariableEffect`'s two all have twelve-slot tables and both middles derive straight from `CEffect`, so nothing above `CStringEffect` introduces it. Shown wrong by: a third `CStringEffect` heir, or a caller.

addresses.name: Effect_GetTargetCountryTag
addresses.signature: CCountryTag* __stdcall Effect_GetTargetCountryTag(CCountryTag* out@stack:4, CEventScope* scope@stack:8, CEffect* effect@ECX) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**Slot 12 of `CWarEffect`, `CWarGoalEffect`, `CModifySpiesEffect` and `CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect`, and the only one of the five slot-12 bodies that is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.** 0x5BD110 to the `ret 8` at 0x5BD215 with an early `ret 8` at 0x5BD14F, 0x106 bytes, eight int3 after. It answers the `CCountryTag` the effect acts on, four ways in priority order:

1. `this->use_this (+0x1C)` set: `EventScope_GetCountryTag(scope)` (0x5C1A40, recorded) - the scope's own subject.
2. `this->use_from (+0x1D)` set: `scope->from_country_tag (+0x18)` and `from_country_id (+0x1C)`.
3. neither, and `this->+0x24 == 0`: the **controller** of the scope's province - `g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790) ->provinces (+0xB8C) [scope->province (+0x28)] ->controller (+0x334)`, which is `CMapProvince +0x334 controller CCountryTag`, *not* `owner (+0x32C)`.
4. otherwise the tag written in the script, held as a `CCountryTag` at `this->+0x20`/`+0x24`.

So `war = { ... }`, `war_goal`, `undeclared_war_region` and `modify_spies` with no country named at all fall through to case 3 and target **whoever currently controls the scoped province** - occupation, not ownership. The class-free name is deliberate (see `slots_noted`): four tables, one address, and no common ancestor among the four but `CEffect`, whose own table has no slot 12.

Nine call sites, in both halves of each class: `CWarEffect::Execute` 0x5BC6FB, `CWarEffect::GetText` 0x5BC9D0 and 0x5BCA83, `CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect::Execute` 0x5BCF28, `CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect::GetText` 0x5BD24E, `CWarGoalEffect::Execute` 0x5BD5E3, `CWarGoalEffect::GetText` 0x5BD6C2, `CModifySpiesEffect::Execute` 0x5BE142, `CModifySpiesEffect::GetText` 0x5BE1DD. Every one of the nine follows the call by reading `scope->country_tag (+0x10)`, i.e. the resolved tag is immediately compared against the acting country.

It also lazily constructs `g_CCurrentGameState` if the global is null - `operator_new(0xDA8)`, `CGameState::CGameState (0x27D070)`, vftable VA 0x15CF674 - which is the same inlined singleton accessor `CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation` and `EventScope_GetCountryTag` carry.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from the vftable entry; both exits are `ret 8` and the signature's two stack dwords agree. Four holders, all at slot 12, from the RTTI tables. The field names are not read off this body: `CEventScope +0x18`/`+0x1C` are `from_country_tag`/`from_country_id`, `+0x28` is `province`, `CMapProvince +0x334` is `controller` and `CCountryTag` is 8 bytes `{char tag[4]; int id}` - all already in project.json's structs, and the body writes `out->+0 = <tag dword>` and `out->+4 = <id dword>` which is exactly that layout. The nine call sites are the per-slot `+0x30` scan over all 43 thirteen-slot classes, each one then read by hand to check that `ecx` is `this` and that exactly two arguments are pushed; the two false positives the scan threw (0x5BBFA6, 0x5BCF9B) are not dispatches and were discarded. Shown wrong by: a fifth holder, or case 3 reading `+0x32C` rather than `+0x334` - the two are 8 bytes apart and the body's displacements are 0x334 and 0x338.

addresses.name: CWarexhaustionEffect::GetText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CWarexhaustionEffect::GetText(CWarexhaustionEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString unread, int unknown)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 9, and one of only two bodies in the whole effect family that uses slot 12 for its text.** 0x59E9A0 to the single `ret 0x28` at 0x59EA43, 0xA6 bytes, ten int3 on both sides. The whole function is: build an `Hoi3CString` holding the literal key `WAREXHAUSTION_EFFECT` (0x15F39E8, length 0x12), dispatch `[vftable+0x30]` - slot 12, `CValueEffect::FormatValueText` - with `out`, `scope` and a pointer to that key, free the key, and return `out` in EAX.

The `Hoi3CString unread` is `CEffect::GetText`'s `group` parameter: 0x1C bytes from `[ebp+0x10]` to `[ebp+0x2B]`, read only to free its heap buffer at 0x59EA25, exactly as the base's own body does. The trailing `int` at `[ebp+0x2C]` is not read at all. 4+4+0x1C+4 = 0x28.

Its twin is `CRevoltRiskEffect::GetText` (0x5A5600), byte-identical but for the key.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; one `ret 0x28`, and the signature's 4+4+0x1C+4 matches both it and the `Hoi3CString`-by-value size of 0x1C that checkSignatures.py already establishes. Held by one table only, `CWarexhaustionEffect` slot 9, so it is not folded. The slot-12 dispatch read instruction by instruction at 0x59E9F2-0x59E9FB: `mov eax,[esi]; mov eax,[eax+0x30]; push edx; push edi; call eax` with `push ecx` of the key one instruction earlier, `edx = [ebp+0xC]`, `edi = [ebp+8]`, `ecx = esi = this`. Shown wrong by: `WAREXHAUSTION_EFFECT` not being a localisation key the game resolves, which a grep of the localisation csv would settle.

addresses.name: CRevoltRiskEffect::GetText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CRevoltRiskEffect::GetText(CRevoltRiskEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString unread, int unknown)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 9, the second and last body in the effect family that uses slot 12.** 0x5A5600 to the single `ret 0x28` at 0x5A56A3, 0xA6 bytes, five int3 before and ten after. The same body as `CWarexhaustionEffect::GetText` (0x59E9A0) but for the key, which is `REVOLTRISK_EFFECT` (0x15F3B38, length 0x11): build the key, dispatch slot 12 - `CValueEffect::FormatValueText` - with `out`, `scope` and the key, free the key, return `out`.

The two of them are what the slot was designed for, and the other nine `CValueEffect` leaves plus all 24 `CIntEffect` leaves duplicate the substitutions in their own slot 9 instead.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; one `ret 0x28` and the signature agrees. One holder only, `CRevoltRiskEffect` slot 9. Dispatch read at 0x5A5652-0x5A565B, the same five instructions as its twin with the same register assignment. A byte compare of the two 0xA6-byte ranges finds exactly nine differing bytes: the key pointer and its length immediate at +0x29..+0x2C, and the three `call rel32` displacements at +0x40, +0x6C and +0x8A, which cannot be equal in two functions at different addresses. Shown wrong by: a tenth differing byte.

addresses.name: CMoneyTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
`money = N`. 0x5F5E70 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F5EB4 and 0x5F5ECE, 0x61 bytes, four int3 before and fifteen after; the two exits are the two arms of one branch and there is no cold path.

    country = CCountryDataBase ([0x1A855A4]) ->+0x16C [scope->country_id (+0x14)]
    pool    = country->government_in_exile (+0x95) ? country + 0x9F8                                  // pool_in_exile
                                                   : CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation(country) + 0x15C  // the province's pool
    return pool->money (+0x10) >= this->value (+0x40)

**That branch is `CCountry::GetPool` (rva 0xF4DE0) inlined, instruction for instruction** - the same `cmp byte ptr [reg+0x95],0; je; lea reg+0x9F8; jmp; call 0x42F100; add eax,0x15C` - so it is nothing special to the trigger: it is the game's one goods-pool accessor, inlined at 40 sites including `CCountry::UpdateIC`, `GetResourceLimitedIC`, `ConsumeIcResources`, `GetAvailableIC`, `CDistributeSupply::Distribute`, `CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel` and `CConvoy::RunDelivery`.

So **a government in exile reads its own stockpile and nobody else's**, and every other country reads the pool physically held on the province `CCountry +0xE24 acting_capital_province_id` names - the acting capital, which falls back when the declared capital at `+0xE20` is lost. A `money` test on an exile never sees its host's money.

Thousandths both sides: `CGoodsPool +0x10` is thousandths and `CValueTrigger`'s slot 7 (0x5D13E0) puts `TokenToFixedPoint(text)` in `+0x40`, so `money = 0.5` is half a unit and the decimal survives. Slot 11 is `CTrigger::CountEvaluation` (0x5D06C0), i.e. it counts as one condition.

One dead store: `mov [esp+8], scope->country_tag (+0x10)` at 0x5F5E8B is never read - the remnant of a `CCountryTag` temporary the compiler optimised into the direct database index.

`CEnergyTrigger`, `CCrudeOilTrigger`, `CRareMaterialsTrigger`, `CMetalTrigger` and `CSuppliesTrigger` are the same 32 instructions at 0x370-byte intervals, differing only in the `CGoodsPool` displacement.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from `CMoneyTrigger`'s vftable slot 6 (table VA 0x15F9034), so both ends are settled without a padding rule: the entry is a table entry and the body ends in fifteen int3. `CCountry::GetPool` (0xF4DE0) decoded alongside it - ten instructions, the identical branch, the identical 0x9F8 and 0x15C displacements and the identical `call 0x42F100` - which is what makes the inlining claim machine-checkable rather than a resemblance. `CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation` re-read to its `ret` at 0x2F1AD: `g_CCurrentGameState->+0xB8C [this->+0xE24]`, a `CMapProvince*`. Every field used was already named in project.json (`CCountry +0x95`, `+0x9F8`, `+0xE24`, `CMapProvince +0x15C`, `CGoodsPool +0x10`) and `CCountry.hpp` documents `+0x95`/`+0x9F8` as the pair; the 40-site count is a scan for `lea reg,[reg+0x9F8]` with a `+0x95` byte compare within 0x20 bytes before and an `add eax,0x15C` within 0x20 after. Shown wrong by: the exile arm reading something other than `+0x9F8`, or a writer that keeps `pool_in_exile` in step with the host's pool - the latter would make the distinction invisible in play and was **not** looked for, which is the gap this entry names.

addresses.name: CEnergyTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `energy = N`. The `CMoneyTrigger::Evaluate` body with one displacement changed: `return pool->energy (+0x1C) >= this->value (+0x40)`, the pool being `CCountry::GetPool` inlined - `pool_in_exile (CCountry +0x9F8)` for a government in exile, the acting capital province's `pool (CMapProvince +0x15C)` otherwise. 0x5F61E0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F6224 and 0x5F623E, 0x61 bytes, thirteen int3 before and fifteen after. Thousandths both sides.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from `CEnergyTrigger`'s vftable slot 6 (table VA 0x15F9068). Byte-for-byte the same 32 instructions as 0x5F5E70 apart from the two `+0x1C` displacements, which is also the 0x370 stride check: the six entries are 0x370 apart **and** sit in six distinct tables 0x34 apart in the same order, so the regularity is six separate bodies and not a linker fold. `CGoodsPool +0x1C energy` was already named. Shown wrong by: `+0x1C` not being `energy` - but then five of the six triggers' displacements would have to be wrong together, since each of the six picks exactly the field its own keyword names.

addresses.name: CCrudeOilTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `crude_oil = N`. The `CMoneyTrigger::Evaluate` body reading `pool->crude_oil (+0x14)` instead: `return pool->+0x14 >= this->value (+0x40)`, over `CCountry::GetPool` inlined. 0x5F6550 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F6594 and 0x5F65AE, 0x61 bytes, thirteen int3 before and fifteen after. Thousandths both sides.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from `CCrudeOilTrigger`'s vftable slot 6 (table VA 0x15F909C); identical to 0x5F5E70 but for the `+0x14` displacements. `CGoodsPool +0x14 crude_oil` was already named. Shown wrong by: a different displacement, which the disassembly shows directly at 0x5F658A and 0x5F65A4.

addresses.name: CRareMaterialsTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `rare_materials = N`. The `CMoneyTrigger::Evaluate` body reading `pool->rare_materials (+0x20)`: `return pool->+0x20 >= this->value (+0x40)`, over `CCountry::GetPool` inlined. 0x5F68C0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F6904 and 0x5F691E, 0x61 bytes, thirteen int3 before and fifteen after. Thousandths both sides.

addresses.comment:
`supplies = N`. The last of the six and the `CMoneyTrigger::Evaluate` body reading `pool->supplies (+0x8)`: `return pool->+0x8 >= this->value (+0x40)`, over `CCountry::GetPool` inlined. 0x5F6FA0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F6FE4 and 0x5F6FFE, 0x61 bytes, thirteen int3 before and fifteen after. **`CGoodsPool` has seven goods and only six of them have a trigger: there is no `fuel` trigger.** The RTTI export has no `CFuelTrigger` while `CFuelPoolEffect` exists, so a script can *set* a country's fuel and cannot *test* it.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from `CSuppliesTrigger`'s vftable slot 6 (table VA 0x15F9138); identical to 0x5F5E70 but for the `+0x8` displacements at 0x5F6FDA and 0x5F6FF4. `CGoodsPool +0x8 supplies` was already named, and `CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel` reaches the same pool through the same inlined `GetPool`.
